thread:
incident-bot: PAGE: Canary anomaly detected for model=rl-13b-v2 on cluster=hosted-us-west1. https://dash.redwood/alerts/2105556666 :error_rate:+6.3% over baseline. Triggered at 2026-03-14T21:11:06Z. Paging #incidents :rotating_light:

Alex B.: On it. I can take first-pass triage. Any initial customer impact? :eyes:

Maya K.: saw the alert—metrics show elevated token rejection and increased 5xxs for streaming endpoints. No SEV page yet but some support tickets flagged latency regressions.

Nina (Support): We have two customers reporting higher latency and partial responses: acct-zenhealth and acct-quickchat. Both on hosted-us-west1. Pings to them sent (trial).

Alex B.: Thanks. Ramon, you're oncall next — want to do handoff?

Ramon G.: Taking over. Quick checklist: (1) confirm alert source, (2) check canary-vs-prod diffs, (3) decide rollback/pin, (4) communicate.

Li S.: Sharing recent canary diff logs I pulled. Paste below — highlights show token-level perplexity spike starting at 21:06Z on rl-13b-v2.

Li S.: ```
[2026-03-14T21:05:58Z] canary/rl-13b-v2 request id=abc123 seq=1 ppls={"avg":6.2, "prev":2.1}
[2026-03-14T21:06:02Z] canary/rl-13b-v2 request id=abc124 seq=1 ppls={"avg":7.9, "prev":2.3}
[2026-03-14T21:06:10Z] canary/rl-13b-v2 internal error: kv-cache-miss, fallback-path applied
[2026-03-14T21:07:01Z] serving/hosted-us-west1 5xx_rate=3.4% (baseline 0.2%)
```

Maya K.: Noted. canary-bot, can you post diffs for the rollout batch (rl-13b-v1 -> rl-13b-v2) around 21:00-21:10Z? Need to see param/quant changes and kernel selection logs.

canary-bot: Posted diff summary: model weights identical on hash, quantization profile changed: int8_fast -> int8_mixed. Kernel selection for attention switched to fast-fused path on Ampere. See snippet: ```kernel_select: attention=fast_fused_v2 (seq_len<=1024)```

Alex B.: okay, that points at quant/profile + fast kernel combo. We've seen fast_fused_v2 exhibit higher KV cache churn in prior tests. Hypothesis A: new quant profile + fused kernel causes more KV cache evictions under streaming workloads leading to retries and 5xx. Hypothesis B: infra regressions (driver upgrade) — need to confirm driver/rt changes in the deployment window.

Ramon G.: I'm pulling node-level driver and runtime logs. deploy-bot, what changed in the canary rollout?

deploy-bot: rollout 2105556600 started at 21:03Z by @sam. Stages: 10% canary -> 30% -> 100% planned. Artifact: rl-13b-v2:sha256:deadbeef. Changed config: quant_profile=int8_mixed, kernel_hint=fast_fused_v2. No infra driver change in this rollout.

Sam (Product Ops): Confirming we kicked the canary at ~21:03Z. No infra driver or kernel package updates in the cluster at that time; only model config changes.

Li S.: I ran a focused repro against canary with streaming sequences >512 and saw repeated KV-cache-miss messages under concurrent streams. Sample run: ```bash
wrk -c 50 -t 4 -d 60s https://hosted-us-west1/generate?model=rl-13b-v2&stream=true
```
Logs show steady increase in latency and occasional process-level GC spikes around miss events.

Alex B.: Customer impact: Nina — are the two reported customers pinned to the new version or subject to rollout traffic split?

Nina (Support): Both were included in the canary traffic by default (no version pinning). They saw partial sequences and reconnects starting at 21:06Z.

Ramon G.: Decision point: Rollback to rl-13b-v1 (safe) or pin problem customers and patch config (riskier). Given 5xx and customer reports, recommend immediate rollback of the canary to v1 for hosted-us-west1. Comments? :thumbsup:

Maya K.: +1 rollback. We should also capture full logs and timeline for RCA.

Alex B.: I'll run rollback command. Executing: ```bash
# rollback canary to rl-13b-v1 on hosted-us-west1
redwoodctl rollout cancel --rollout-id 2105556600 --force && redwoodctl deploy set-default --model rl-13b-v1 --region hosted-us-west1
```

deploy-bot: Rollback started at 2026-03-14T21:12:14Z. Canary traffic shifted back to rl-13b-v1. Health checks passing at 21:13:02Z. 5xx rate dropped to 0.4% by 21:15:00Z.

Ramon G.: Good. Immediate mitigation done. Now in-incident RCA coordination: we need a timeline, evidence, and a controlled repro plan. I'll collect kernel logs and KV cache metrics for the 21:00-21:10 window and attach to the ticket.

Li S.: Attaching extracted metrics: ```
kv_cache.evictions: 2100 (rl-13b-v2 canary window)
kv_cache.evictions: 120 (rl-13b-v1 baseline window)
stream.concurrent_retries: spike at 21:06Z to 18/min
```

Alex B.: Action items captured inline: 1) Full log bundle upload to S3 (s3://redwood-incidents/2105556666/logs) — Li to upload. 2) Reproduce in staging with quant_profile=int8_mixed + fast_fused_v2 under streaming load — Alex to run. 3) Engineering: add guard in rollout pipeline to block quant_profile/kernel combos not seen in canary test matrix — Ramon + Maya. 4) Support: notify affected customers with incident summary — Nina.

Sam (Product Ops): Also verify version pinning behavior: why were customers not pinned? We should add quick checklist to include 'exempt critical customers from canary' opt-in.

Nina (Support): Draft sent to impacted accounts. No major revenue impact reported so far; tickets open and being handled.

canary-bot: Canaries reverted at 21:13:02Z. Canary health status: OK on rl-13b-v1. Please link RCA ticket: RED-INC-2105556666.

Ramon G.: We'll keep this thread as the working in-incident RCA until we create the formal doc. I'll post a preliminary timeline after log collection. For now, marking incident mitigated and moving to postmortem prep. :white_check_mark:
